about.title: Fencing that keeps a Baytown property secure, private and good looking.
text: Fencing plays an important role in enhancing security and privacy for properties in Baytown, TX. With the increasing instances of trespassing and theft, a sturdy fence can deter potential intruders and protect your belongings, and it gives you and your family a sense of safety in your own outdoor space.

A fence does more than close a boundary. A carefully chosen and well-designed one adds to the look of your landscape, and it can act as a noise barrier, keeping the sound of the street out and making the space inside your property quieter.

We install wood, aluminum, chain link and pool fencing and electric gates. We know the local regulations and building codes, we work with quality materials and tools, and we handle the digging, the posts and the panels so you do not have to take the job on yourself.
about.imageAlt: A wrought iron automatic driveway gate between stone columns at the end of a gravel drive

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Baytown?
faqs.a: In Baytown a permit is typically needed for any new fence installation, whatever its size or location. The local building or zoning department confirms what your project needs, and the approval can take time, so it is worth starting early.

faqs.q: How tall can my fence be?
faqs.a: The maximum height allowed in residential areas is typically six feet, though it can vary with your neighborhood or zoning. Some neighborhoods also set rules for where a fence can sit, such as setbacks from property lines or roads.

faqs.q: What does Baytown require around a swimming pool?
faqs.a: Pool barriers or fences must be at least four feet high with self-closing and self-latching gates, and the gate should be locked when the pool is not in use.

faqs.q: Which fencing material suits Baytown's weather?
faqs.a: The hot, humid weather here is hard on some materials. Cedar, cypress and redwood naturally resist rot and decay, aluminum resists corrosion, rust and fading, and vinyl will not rot, peel or fade. Wood needs more regular maintenance than the others.

faqs.q: How much maintenance does a fence need?
faqs.a: Inspect it regularly for loose boards, broken pickets, rust spots or bent posts, and clean it: wood with mild soap and water, metal with a gentle scrub. Wood also needs a protective sealant or stain to keep moisture, mold and rot out.

faqs.q: How do I get a price?
faqs.a: Call us or fill in the free estimate form with your name, email, phone and address. Ask for a written estimate that covers materials, labor and anything specific to your property.

facts.heading: Choosing a Fencing Material
items: Start with the purpose: privacy, security, containing children and pets, or the look of the place
Baytown's hot, humid weather and heavy rain are hard on some materials, so pick one that stands up to it with little upkeep
Materials vary a lot in cost, so pick one that fits the budget
Decide how much maintenance you are willing to do: wood needs more regular care and repair than vinyl, composite or metal
Check your neighborhood's or homeowners' association rules on height, location and design before you choose

facts.heading: What Affects the Price
items: The size of the area being fenced, because a bigger run takes more material and more labor
The height of the fence: a taller one takes more material and sometimes extra support
The material: galvanized steel chain link is generally cheaper than vinyl-coated, which resists rust better and looks better
The layout of the property, the terrain and how complicated the installation is
The number of gates and the type of gate, which on an electric gate means swing, sliding or bi-fold
The long run as well as the day one price, because a cheaper fence that needs frequent repair can cost more in the end
We recommend getting detailed written quotes from several Baytown companies and comparing them side by side, each covering materials, labor and anything specific to your property

facts.heading: Looking After Your Fence
items: Inspect it regularly for loose or broken boards and pickets, rust spots, bent or damaged posts, cracked panels and loose screws and bolts, and fix what you find early
Wood: clean with mild soap and water, and keep a protective sealant or stain on it to hold out moisture, mold and rot
Metal and chain link: a gentle scrub with a wire brush or soft brush and water, then rinse off the residue
Aluminum: mild soap, or water and vinegar, with no abrasive cleaner or tool that would scratch it, then rinse and dry with a soft cloth
Vinyl: mild detergent and water
Clear vegetation growing against the fence, since it can weaken the foundation, and watch for algae and mildew building up
Baytown's humidity makes metal fences more prone to rust, so inspect them more often
Wood: clear leaves, dirt and debris with a soft brush or a low-pressure power washer, and reapply the sealant or stain every few years
Trim overhanging branches so they cannot scratch the fence, and keep sprinklers and other water sources off the wood, which causes water damage and warping
Watch for pests in a wood fence and treat them with a non-toxic deterrent, or an insecticide if it comes to that; wood can be prone to rot and termite damage
Aluminum: clean it at least once a year, look for scratches, dents and cracked or chipped paint, and let it dry fully before any touch-up or protective coating
Wrought iron needs regular maintenance to keep rust off it

facts.heading: Pool Fence Inspection Checklist
items: Check the panels, posts and gate hardware for wear, tighten loose screws and bolts and replace anything broken or cracked
Check the gate still swings, closes and latches smoothly, and that the hinges and latches work
Clean the fence with mild detergent and water, scrubbing stubborn stains gently with a soft brush
Clear any vegetation or obstruction growing near the fence

facts.heading: How a Fence Goes In
items: The fence line is marked out with string or stakes, set straight and level, and checked against trees, rocks, slopes and anything already standing
The ground is cleared of debris, vegetation and rocks so the run is level
Post holes are dug to a depth set by the height of the fence and the soil, and the posts are cemented in and left to set
Rails go on, then the panels or, on a chain link fence, the fabric stretched tight with tension and brace bands
The gate is hung from the adjoining posts and the finished fence is inspected
The perimeter and the height are measured carefully, so the finished run has no gaps or uneven sections
Underground utility lines and the property boundaries are checked before a post hole is dug, so nothing is damaged and nothing encroaches on the neighbors
The ground is levelled and compacted so the posts do not shift or sink later
On a privacy fence the holes are dug deep enough to take about a third of the length of the post, and the posts are set plumb and level in concrete and left to dry

facts.heading: Choosing a Fence Installer
items: Look for an installer with a track record in the kind of fence you want, read online reviews, and ask friends or neighbors who have had one put in recently
Check credentials and certifications, and that the installer carries the licenses and insurance the work calls for
Arrange a consultation or site visit with more than one installer, and ask about their experience, the materials and techniques they use, and the timeline and the cost
Ask to see samples of work they have already done
Ask for a detailed written estimate covering materials, labor and any additional services
Ask what warranty or guarantee covers the workmanship
Notice how they communicate, whether they listen to what you want and whether they will customize the fence to it

facts.heading: Alternatives to a Wood Fence
items: Vinyl: durable and low maintenance, resistant to rot, insects and water damage, which suits Baytown's humid climate, and made in a range of styles and colors, privacy and picket among them
Wrought iron: a classic, elegant look, strong and long lasting, good for security and privacy, and able to carry decorative scrollwork or finials

facts.heading: Ideas for Working a Fence into the Yard
items: A fence as the backdrop to a garden, with flower beds or potted plants in front of it, framing the planting and giving it some structure
A fence around a patio or seating area to mark it off and make it private, which helps on a large open lot or where the neighbors are close
Outdoor plants and hanging decor on a privacy fence, or flower boxes and climbing vines on a chain link one
